chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a dog that fled and was not sent by its owner, so it hunted, and its owner caught up with it and it had killed the prey. Can he eat from it? He said: No.

And he (peace be upon him) said: When it hunts and has been named (Bismillah), let him eat; and if it hunts and has not been named, let him not eat. And this is from what you have taught the hunting animals, trained ones.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat from a dog that hunted on its own without being sent by the owner?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the condition of *tasmiyah* (reciting God's name) for the validity of game hunted by trained dogs, distinguishing between the dog's inherent training and the owner's specific invocation. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the hunter's conscious act of sanctifying the kill, ensuring the meat is halal only when the divine name is explicitly mentioned at the time of sending the beast. It reflects the broader principle that the permissibility of hunted meat relies on the proper ritual invocation by the owner, linking physical action with spiritual intent.
